samples.question: The picture shows a grey metal plate lying on white paper. Two white holes are punched right through the plate, so the plate has an outer rim and two hole rims. Three coloured bands are painted across the plate - one red, one green and one blue. Each band is a single unbroken strip that starts on a rim, wanders across the grey and ends on a rim; the bands never touch each other, and away from its two ends a band never touches any rim. Now imagine cutting the plate with scissors along ONE of the coloured bands, all the way from one end of that band to the other, and nowhere else: the grey under that band is removed, and the other two bands are only paint and are not cut along. Two bits of grey belong to the same piece when grey still joins them after the cut. Exactly one of the three bands falls the plate into two separate pieces; cutting along either of the other two leaves the plate in one single piece. Which band falls the plate into two pieces - red, green or blue?
